cells.tense: You are here at the seed, and the meetings you are in are real ones, chosen rather than stumbled into.
cells.ask: offer the next piece of yourself without checking first whether it will be matched
cells.core:
At the seed there is no end of possible meetings, and you are not grabbing at all of them. You can tell which current is worth entering and you enter it, and two things that were moving separately begin to move as one. This is what it looks like when it goes well here: the field stays open because you are not trying to close it, and you move in it lightly, near what is real without clutching at it.

What keeps this alive is the same thing that started it: the meeting only stays real if you keep bringing yourself to it. Choosing is not a single moment you did once and can rest on — it is offered again today, and taking it again is what lets the current keep carrying you somewhere new.
cells.sheetLine: You meet what's worth meeting and choose it on purpose, and it flows.
cells.verb: meeting a real current and choosing to flow with it, two becoming one
cells.place: at the seed, where everything is possible and nothing has been decided yet

cells.tense: You are already living in a version of this meeting that hasn't happened yet, and you are arranging yourself around it ahead of time.
cells.ask: let one thing grow at the pace it's actually growing, and leave it alone for a day
cells.core:
At the seed there is every possible meeting at once, and in good shape that is a wide open field you can stand in without needing to close it. The meeting you want is not here yet, and you are already acting as if it were — merging ahead of time with something only imagined, feeling your way toward a bond no one has entered.

The trouble is not the wanting. It is that the joining runs ahead of the meeting, so nothing gets to arrive as itself. What is there to tend tends to grow without being pushed — care that does not exhaust, holding without gripping — and it can only be found by standing where the seed actually is rather than where you have already decided it will go.
cells.sheetLine: You've already joined something that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.verb: meeting a real current and choosing to flow with it, two becoming one
cells.place: at the seed, where everything is possible and nothing has been decided yet

cells.tense: You met something real and stepped back from it, and you are still standing at that distance, where the joining was and is no longer.
cells.ask: give one plain thing you notice about the meeting to someone who is in it, and let it stand without proof
cells.core:
At the seed every meeting is still open, and in good shape that is room, not danger — you can be near something real and let it show you what it is. You stepped out of the joining, and the open field stopped being a place to move in.

What is missing is not the ability to bond. It is the willingness to say what you already perceive — your read of the thing lands, and you keep negotiating with it as if it hadn't. When what you know is allowed the weight it already has, the meeting can begin to look solid again; you don't have to believe it, only say it to one person and see how it holds.
cells.sheetLine: You pulled back from a real meeting and stayed back.

cells.tense: The joining is underway right now, here at the seed, and you are describing it as though it were happening on its own.
cells.ask: take one small practice, done alone and without an audience, and let it be the thing that steadies the meeting
cells.core:
At the seed there is no end of possible meetings, and the one you are in is already shaping how you move and what you say. It is real, and it is yours. Yet the way you tell it, a current caught you — as if you had not walked toward it.

The joining is alive in you and you have not claimed it as your own doing. Something quieter than the meeting can return it — a small thing done on your own, steady and unfussed, which is how an unclear direction finds its way back to ground. Solitude that connects rather than isolates is the simplest form of it, and it belongs to you whether or not anyone sees you do it.
cells.sheetLine: The meeting is already real. You haven't owned that you chose it.
